summary.name: SRE Classroom: Distributed PubSub
summary.one_liner: A Google SRE workshop that teaches non-abstract large system design (NALSD) by having participants design and evaluate a publish-subscribe messaging system against performance, correctness and SLO requirements.
use_cases: Teaching NALSD principles to developers and SREs
Running a group workshop on designing a pub/sub system
Practicing distributed system design against SLOs
Learning how to evaluate performance and correctness trade-offs in messaging systems
Reusing Google SRE workshop slides for training
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a workshop developed by Google's Site Reliability Engineering group. It opens with theory on design principles such as correctness, reliability, performance and inter-system communication styles, then has participants build a publish-subscribe system that meets stated performance, correctness and SLO requirements. The workshop ends with a detailed example solution and a discussion of the system's inputs and SLOs. Participant and facilitator resources and slides are linked from the page.
notable: Hands-on group exercise designed for groups of five, scaling from 1 to 20 groups
Materials released under CC-BY-4.0 with Google credited as author
Includes slides, participant resources and facilitator resources
caveats: Designed as an in-person or facilitated workshop; the page does not describe a self-paced version
Page lists materials but the page text itself contains no detailed solution content
